title: Master Directory of Global and National Reports, Indexes, and Rankings

indexes.dimensions: 1. Long and healthy life (Life expectancy at birth), 2. Knowledge (Expected years of schooling & Mean years of schooling), 3. Decent standard of living (GNI per capita in PPP $)
indexes.key_fact: Conceptualized in 1990 by Pakistani economist Mahbub ul Haq and Indian Nobel laureate Amartya Sen.

indexes.dimensions: Economic Participation and Opportunity, Educational Attainment, Health and Survival, Political Empowerment
indexes.key_fact: Assesses gender parity. Global score indicates it will take over a century to achieve full parity.

indexes.indicators: 1. Undernourishment (1/3 weight), 2. Child Stunting (1/6 weight), 3. Child Wasting (1/6 weight), 4. Child Mortality (1/3 weight)
indexes.top_ranking_country: Belarus, Bosnia & Herzegovina, Chile (among lowest hunger group)
indexes.key_fact: India categorizes in the 'Serious' hunger severity band with score ~27.3.

indexes.dimensions: Innovation Inputs (Institutions, Human capital, Infrastructure, Market sophistication, Business sophistication) and Innovation Outputs (Knowledge & tech outputs, Creative outputs)
indexes.top_ranking_country: Switzerland (#1 for 14th consecutive year), followed by Sweden and USA
indexes.key_fact: India jumped from 81st position in 2015 to top 40 in 2024-2026, leading lower-middle income economies.

indexes.publishing_organization: Reporters Without Borders (Reporters Sans Frontieres - RSF, Paris)
indexes.indicators: Political context, Legal framework, Economic context, Sociocultural context, Safety of journalists
indexes.key_fact: Norway has retained the top position for 8 consecutive years.

indexes.variables: GDP per capita, Social support, Healthy life expectancy, Freedom to make life choices, Generosity, Perceptions of corruption
indexes.top_ranking_country: Finland (#1 for 7th consecutive year), followed by Denmark and Iceland
indexes.key_fact: Published annually on International Day of Happiness (20th March).
Assesses perceived levels of public sector corruption based on 13 data sources.

indexes.dimensions: Customs clearance efficiency, Quality of trade & transport infrastructure, Ease of arranging competitively priced shipments, Competence of logistics services, Tracking & tracing, Timeliness
indexes.key_fact: India's rank improved from 54th (2014) to 38th supported by PM Gati Shakti and National Logistics Policy.

indexes.publishing_organization: Henley & Partners (based on official data from IATA)
indexes.top_ranking_country: Singapore (#1 with visa-free access to 195 destinations)

indexes.dimensions: Health (Nutrition, Child & Adolescent mortality, Maternal health), Education (Years of schooling, School attendance), Standard of Living (Cooking fuel, Sanitation, Drinking water, Electricity, Housing, Assets, Bank Account)
indexes.key_findings: Multidimensional poverty in India declined from 29.17% (2013-14) to 11.28% (2022-23); 24.82 crore people exited multidimensional poverty. Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, and Madhya Pradesh registered fastest reductions.
indexes.top_performing_state: Kerala has the lowest proportion of multidimensionally poor citizens (0.55%).

indexes.top_performing_states: Larger States: 1. Gujarat, 2. Kerala, 3. Punjab. Smaller States: Goa. UTs: Chandigarh.
